custom_upstream_file_changes.change: Add native selected-furniture infrastructure configuration forms stored through the editor's undoable Building.mods extension data; context-sensitive recorder, camera, router/AP and switch settings with existing HA entity pickers and channel duplicate protection.
Build and fingerprint a separately lazy-loaded infrastructure manager entry bundle with an independent size budget; include it in watch and production builds.

Add the downstream, separately bundled infrastructure manager UI for inventory, camera configuration, recorder capacity/channel assignments, network interfaces, switch port assignments, IP inventory/CSV, logical topology, connections and validation; persist through Building.mods and editor events.
Load the infrastructure manager by a cache-busted dynamic import only when requested.
Add an Infrastructure Manager Extensions entry and lazy-loaded manager route with equipment locate return path.
Add a compact selected-infrastructure action to open the lazy manager and accept manager edits through the editor undo history.
Generated lazy manager bundle, separate from the editor and main bundles.
Extend the approved executable module field contract with a plain text input field for hostnames, addresses and metadata; the furniture-only signing restriction is unchanged.
Add optional Building.mods data, reusing the existing module namespace for backward-compatible plan persistence and standard export/import.
Add the native context-sensitive infrastructure furniture form and undoable metadata mutations; delete/duplicate operations maintain connected infrastructure references.

Add camera horizontal/vertical FOV, full-circle azimuth, coverage color/opacity and optional ground projection controls; keep selected camera elevation synchronized with its furniture geometry and carry azimuth through furniture rotation.
Merge infrastructure camera furniture metadata with bound native camera markers and carry the furniture lens pose/FOV into the native stream marker without creating duplicate camera markers.

Render a per-floor translucent 3D CCTV frustum and optional native ground projection from the camera lens pose; persistent Show-menu visibility is separate from spotlight cone visibility and follows floor Apart/Stacked transforms.
Add persistent Camera field of view control to the Show menu, disabled by default.
Extend optional camera metadata with color, opacity and ground projection settings and calculate camera furniture lens poses from depth, height, azimuth and floor elevation.
Add a plain-text field to the approved module editor API for separately approved executable extensions.
Add optional Building.mods extension metadata for compatible save/export/import.
Regenerated editor bundle for optional infrastructure configuration forms; passed existing size budget.

Add isolated optional infrastructure inventory types and pure validation/summary helpers for IP, MAC, network-scoped duplicate warnings and estimated camera coverage; stored in the approved module namespace.
Regression coverage for address validation, network-scoped duplicate detection, missing connection references and bounded estimated camera coverage.
Furniture-only source for CCTV/network equipment. Sign with the existing restricted TechPanda key; this authorizes no executable module code.
Optional downstream inventory UI source using the separately approved NeonPlan module workflow; it is not embedded in or authorized by the furniture-only pack.
Ignore local integration backups and generated furniture pack/preview output so secrets and local artifacts are not staged accidentally. No upstream runtime behavior changes.
Add TechPanda Ed25519 public key 4d62b4e84557 to PACK_PUBLIC_KEYS and the same id to STUDIO_KEYS, restricting it to studio.* furniture-only packs with no Pro features or executable module.
Set the downstream HACS version from techpanda/release.json (currently 4.0.2.4b3, based on upstream 4.0.2); update this value for each reviewed downstream prerelease or stable release.
Regenerated to report downstream version 4.0.2.2 and load the TechPanda solar visibility implementation.
Regenerated for downstream version 4.0.2.2 and matching frontend asset fingerprints.
Add a default-enabled Solar Panels control to the existing Show menu in multi-floor Property View and persist the device preference through the existing prefs store.
Forward the Property View solar preference to the viewer while forcing existing individual-floor behavior to remain enabled.
Add German and English Solar Panels menu labels and hint text.
Route existing garden and wall solar primitives into separate per-floor buffers rather than the merged walls/furniture buffers.
Route existing roof solar primitives into separate per-roof-part buffers using the native pushModules renderer.
Add independently hideable batched solar layers and route composed ground-face arrays to their source plan floor; preserve native live overlays and keep solar placement independent of roof lift/fade.
Assert floor-mounted solar buffers remain separate from walls, furniture and shared line geometry.
Assert native roof solar geometry is separated from roof body triangles and edge lines.

Add deterministic Property View solar enabled/disabled preview shots and a preference reload assertion; identify known optional preview-only missing-pack and favicon 404s without masking other browser errors.
Regenerated native viewer bundle containing the independently toggleable solar geometry layers.
Regenerated with synchronized frontend strings and downstream asset fingerprints.
Compose secondary site-plan solar fields and strings into read-only Property View, transform their placement and references, and retain a runtime floor association for ground-face arrays.
Add optional runtime-only siteFloorId metadata to SolarField for Property View floor routing; it is not persisted in plan storage.
Cover secondary roof-field composition and live bindings, plus site-transformed ground-array position, rotation, elevation and native floor-geometry generation.

Render the shared-Three infrastructure route overlay from data supplied by the lazy manager, expose equipment/label visibility controls, and split CCTV/network furniture geometry into independently visible and pickable batches.
Batch CCTV furniture and network equipment into separate buffers so their visibility can be controlled independently while preserving item pick ranges.

Estimate cable path lengths from actual floor elevations, produce route segments, recognize equipment item ids stored in signed furniture pack types, and validate switch port/PoE and recorder channel allocations. Bullet CCTV furniture coverage anchors now start at the redesigned analog/IP bullet lens plane; other camera models keep the existing pose rule.
Forward independent Wi-Fi and network-connection visibility preferences to the native viewer. Pass the furniture type into the camera pose helper for bullet lens alignment.
Add persistent, default-off Show controls for estimated Wi-Fi and network connection geometry.
Suppress the generic selected-furniture wireframe ghost for only the TechPanda Wi-Fi router and access point pack item types; furniture selection, hit testing and editing remain active.
Cover the targeted furniture selection ghost policy: router and access point are suppressed while other furniture types keep their wireframe.
Load the Smart RGB manager chunk on demand through a cache-busted dynamic import.

Define versioned furniture.mods configuration, stable fixture IDs, explicitly assigned entity bindings and firmware zone mapping; new fixtures start unbound, saved explicit bindings and sparse/empty LED edge maps remain intact, and implicit wall mounting matches the native pack default.

Classify Smart RGB pack fixtures as decorative self-illuminating devices, never conventional lamps, even if a legacy or malformed pack definition includes lamp metadata; ordinary lamp classification is unchanged.

Refresh native RGB furniture geometry and animation state when its bound Home Assistant light, sensor, pattern, brightness, speed or colour state changes; restore the saved plan configuration after asynchronous lazy-runtime loading and refresh native floor geometry after lazy renderer registration even when the plan key is unchanged.
Allow explicitly narrow module line widths so animated RGB flow ribbons can match physical LED strips instead of using the much wider energy-cable minimum.

Expose refreshFurniture() to rebuild the native viewer geometry for the current shown plan after an isolated lazy furniture renderer registers, bypassing same-plan-key update suppression without changing plan data.
Generate bounded shared-edge hex and triangular panel/groove layout geometry.

Render only configured RGB strip geometry through native viewer buffers. No entity binding means neutral charcoal and no animation; bound entities must report on with valid colour and nonzero brightness. Multizone edges require their own zone-on report or explicit active zone entity. Active effect ribbons use the native narrow, non-additive pipe layer rather than additive energy-cable halos, and remain aligned with physical strips. Smart RGB does not emit room lighting. The isolated lazy bundle keeps stable furniture-local transforms and does not rely on a duplicate main-bundle pack registry.
Call existing Home Assistant entity services from the isolated Smart RGB manager; no direct browser-to-controller calls.
Add the lazy editor for fixture layouts, raised panels, assigned RGB edges, bindings, and HA service controls.
Register the Smart RGB runtime and manager in the independently lazy-loaded bundle.
Allow the native furniture builder to consume the Smart RGB triangle geometry callback.
Cover unbound defaults, retained explicit bindings, firmware zone mappings, sanitization, persistence across plan cloning, and saved sparse/empty edge maps.
Cover connected-hex shared edges, triangular layout/grooves, and bounded geometry generation.

Cover strict unbound/off/unavailable/zero-brightness behavior, per-zone state and brightness, neutral geometry, pipe-only non-additive animation, exclusion from conventional room lighting, retained ordinary lamp behavior, exact strip alignment across transforms, and rendering when the lazy bundle has no shared pack registry.
Verify Home Assistant service routing and no-op behavior for unavailable/unconfigured entities.

Generated isolated Smart RGB manager and viewer bundle (52.3 KB); package at integration frontend root and load on demand. Viewer geometry resolves without cross-bundle pack registry state. Explicit entity/state gating renders inactive fixtures charcoal; animated strips use the narrow non-additive pipe layer.
Regenerated native viewer bundle for narrow Smart RGB pipe widths; keeps decorative RGB strips out of the additive energy-cable layer.
Regenerated for decorative Smart RGB fixtures to remain excluded from conventional room-light classification while normal lamps are unchanged.
Allow the existing furniture mounting-height control to accept the backend-supported -5 m lower bound for below-ground placement.
Clamp saved furniture mounting heights to the backend-supported -5 m to 10 m range.
Regenerated main frontend bundle for the existing furniture mounting control's below-ground range and bounded save normalization.

Pass the persisted underground inspection state into the viewer and rebuild live state on toggle changes.
Export the stable underground tank type and preserve normalized negative mount height through existing furniture support.
Build temporary localized floor holes above underground tank footprints and suppress underground furniture geometry when inspection is off.

Lazy-load tank inspection helpers, rebuild floor cutouts, gate underground visuals and water on valid sensor readings, animate live level geometry until it reaches sensor targets, and preserve floor-local transforms.

Build underground tank bodies and cyan boundary lines in separate per-floor geometry buffers during inspection so only the tank can use translucent materials and correct rotated footprints.
Render underground tank inspection geometry translucently, retain floor-local transforms and picking, and focus a selected tank from an elevated isometric camera.
Expose the viewer focus action for an existing underground tank without changing plan data.
